hypotheses.observation: capacity_summary is BOUNDED with lower_inclusive 237 and upper_exclusive 357; step-1 PASS (target 120, verified_bound_load 117), step-2 PASS (target 240, verified_bound_load 237), step-3 FAIL (target 360, verified_bound_load 357) with windowed policy check response_time_p95_ms observed 420 > threshold 250.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The first latency policy failure occurs at the highest user count, consistent with the system losing the ability to hold p95 latency at or below 250 ms somewhere between the last verified-passing load (237 users) and the verified-failing load (357 users).
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run additional load steps inside (237, 357), e.g., 260/280/300/320 users, with the same 250 ms p95 rule to locate the transition point, and enable a knee detector to replace knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

hypotheses.observation: Overall metric summaries (overall and checkout JMETER_SAMPLER) report max 1500 ms, p99 420 ms, p95 417 ms, p50 136 ms, with error_count 0 and error_rate 0/3601; the stage-3 window p95 is 420 ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The degradation is concentrated in the latency tail (p95/p99 ≈ 420 ms) while the overall p50 is 136 ms and a small number of samples reach 1500 ms, suggesting queueing, GC, or transient contention on a minority of requests rather than a uniform slowdown.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Extract per-sample latency and per-10s-bin p95 for stage-3 and correlate the slowest samples with server-side GC/queue/CPU evidence before attributing the failure to sustained saturation.

hypotheses.possible_explanation: The load generator was not CPU-bound in any window, so generator CPU saturation is an unlikely cause of the stage-3 latency failure; however, only generator CPU is evidenced, leaving generator memory/threads/network and all SUT-side resources unmeasured.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect generator memory/thread/network metrics plus SUT-side CPU, memory, I/O, and DB/queue depth during stage-3 to rule out non-CPU bottlenecks before narrowing the cause to the system under test.

hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization (e.g., NTP offset) across the load generator, SUT, and analysis host, then re-check window alignment before any lead/lag or temporal causal interpretation.
